digest.component_or_area: plan-review criteria vocabulary and detector logic
propositions: Success Criteria and Acceptance Criteria headings carry identical semantic intent across all live criteria gates but are treated as separate vocabulary, preventing SC items from counting toward P1 floor and blocking checkbox validation

SC criteria are conventionally written as plain bullets rather than checkboxes, making them invisible to _count_ac_items counting logic and unable to carry [operator-attested] tags, while AC items under checkboxes are individually verifiable

The vocabulary split is vestigial and actively harmful—every criterion that touches both pools them under one bar, with no live semantic axis differentiating them, so collapsing to single Acceptance Criteria heading tightens the gate without changing intent

Store migration requires moving 106 existing tickets from ## Success Criteria heading (plain bullets) to ## Acceptance Criteria heading (checkboxes), regenerating the criteria guide from updated registry, and updating all detector regexes and reviewer prompts to recognize single heading only

Three live source files must permanently exclude Success Criteria vocabulary from renaming: plan_review_T2.md (pilot metrics context, not heading semantics), plan_review_verifier.md and plan_review_verifier_agentic.md (dod_uncertifiable definition, separate concept deferred by scope), and llm/completion.py bearing heading-sense language requires sweeping even though no child story owned it
